scope_note: This is the 2026-09-06 corrective pass responding to the 4th independent Codex rejection of PR #5620 (head 32e63b78a), which found 8 must-fix defects. Each is fixed with real code changes (not test-only workarounds): (1) target authorization/system scope — RegistryEntry now carries an immutable owner_tenant bound at creation from the verified creating caller's tenant claim (never client-suppliable); every read/list/write route now requires a verified caller (GET routes were previously anonymous) and enforces tenant-scoped access via _authorize_read/_authorize_write; a reserved BUILTIN_TENANT identity marks checked-in bootstrap artifacts as publicly readable but never caller-mutable, and a caller can never assert that reserved tenant value. (2) fail-closed configuration — once the durable Postgres backend is selected, auth must be explicitly strict with a configured issuer+audience or the service fails closed (500) rather than silently accepting an unsigned structured token or a strict token with no expected issuer/audience; a configured DSN with an unset/memory backend also fails closed instead of silently running against the in-memory test double. (3) genuine positive capabilities — POST /api/registry/entries now supports a name-only draft ({'name': '...'}) with a stable synthesized strategy identity in addition to the full typed body; the StrategySpec facade's checksum is now computed from, and metadata.strategy_spec is always bound to, the exact persisted payload (no setdefault divergence); the generic metadata PATCH can no longer introduce a reserved key (strategy_spec/strategy_artifact/allocation_policy_artifact/source_seed_id) that never existed on the entry, only change/remove an existing one (both now rejected). (4) immutable revision identity — register_if_absent enforces a real atomic (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) uniqueness at the store layer (PostgresJsonOwnerStore.insert_if_absent's unique_fields table lock / RegistryStore's process lock), so two different caller-supplied registry_ids can no longer both commit at the same version; a parent-linked revision must be a strictly greater version than its linked parent (no downgrade). (5) actual durable Strategy readback and ambiguity — the BFF StrategyCommandAdapter now performs a genuine scoped owner GET after every metadata PATCH and verifies checksum/updated_at/metadata against what the PATCH response claimed before reporting success; on an ambiguous/empty PATCH response it attempts the readback to distinguish 'committed but response lost' (readback confirms) from 'not committed/unconfirmed' (readback doesn't confirm or errors) instead of an immediate hard failure. (6) replay semantics — the metadata-CAS replay digest now covers the caller's precondition (expected_metadata) as well as the target metadata, so a same-key request with a changed precondition is a divergent replay (409) even when the target metadata coincidentally matches; DivergentCommandReplayError is now caught and mapped to 409 (was an unhandled 500); the receipt key is now built by length-prefixing each component before hashing, so tenant/actor values containing the prior delimiter can no longer collide. (7) receipts/crash-window verification — create_if_absent's atomic table-locked identity reservation already gives idempotent-replay correctness for creates (re-issuing the same registry_id after a lost response returns the identical canonical entry); this pass adds direct proof of that property plus the atomic-uniqueness proof under HTTP, but does not add a new receipts-table write for the create path specifically (see acceptance_check and not_covered_in_this_delivery for the precise, honest boundary) or a full outbox/prepare-activate-reconcile crash-window harness. (8) scope/process — the orchestrating session reworked the initial implementation of items 1 and 3's builtin-actor binding so it lands entirely inside already-declared files (split_api.py's register_if_absent now defaults an absent actor to a reserved bootstrap identity, instead of editing the undeclared strategy_artifact.py directly), and merged the new regression-test module directly into the already-declared test_service.py instead of adding a new undeclared test file — so every file this generation-5 pass touches is within the existing declared artifact contract (see files_modified below, files_added is empty). Five files from an earlier generation (conftest.py, test_owner_durability_real_process.py, test_registry_auth_wiring.py, test_registry_positives.py, test_storage_backend_posture.py — see files_not_yet_declared_in_artifact_contract_from_prior_generation) remain genuinely undeclared and unchanged by this pass; only Human/Ops can run the governed artifact-contract add, so this task records a blocker requesting that before re-handoff rather than silently expanding scope.

summary: models.py: added BUILTIN_TENANT reserved-identity constant and RegistryEntry.owner_tenant (immutable, set once at creation from the verified creating actor's tenant claim, serialized in to_dict/from_dict).

storage.py / pg_store.py: _new_entry now binds owner_tenant from the actor. create_if_absent gained a unique_fields parameter (RegistryStore: in-process scan under the existing lock; PostgresRegistryStore: passed through to PostgresJsonOwnerStore.insert_if_absent's table-locked composite-identity check) so register_if_absent can enforce atomic (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) uniqueness across different registry_ids. build_registry_store() now also fails closed when REGISTRY_STORE_DSN/DATABASE_URL is configured but the backend resolves to memory (a configured DSN with a silently-memory-selected backend previously looked like a working deployment while every write vanished). pg_store.py's receipt_key now length-prefixes and hashes its components (was a plain colon-join, ambiguous when tenant/actor values themselves contain a colon); the metadata-CAS request digest now covers expected_metadata (the caller's precondition) in addition to new_metadata.

split_api.py: register()/register_if_absent() call a new _reject_version_collision / pass unique_fields respectively; update_metadata() now catches DivergentCommandReplayError and maps it to RegistryConflictError (409) instead of letting it propagate as an unhandled 500; _reject_immutable_metadata_mutation now rejects introducing a reserved key that never existed (previously only rejected changing/removing an already-present one).

service.py: every read route (get_entry, list_entries, get_strategy_spec_entry, list_strategy_spec_entries, get_strategy_artifact_entry, list_strategy_artifact_entries, get_allocation_policy_artifact_entry, list_allocation_policy_artifacts, latest_approved, deployment_view) now requires a verified caller via a new _authenticate_registry_read, and single-entry reads/writes call _authorize_read/_authorize_write to enforce tenant scoping and builtin-write denial. A new _require_production_auth_configuration fails closed (500) once the Postgres backend is selected unless auth is explicitly strict with issuer+audience configured. _reject_reserved_tenant_claim denies a caller asserting the BUILTIN_TENANT value. POST /api/registry/entries now accepts a name-only draft via a new RegistryEntryOrDraftRequest/_resolve_entry_or_draft_payload. _strategy_spec_register_payload now always binds metadata['strategy_spec'] to the checksummed payload (was metadata.setdefault, which could diverge from a caller-supplied metadata.strategy_spec). _validate_strategy_spec_version_lineage now requires a parent-linked version to be strictly greater than the linked parent's version. _ensure_strategy_spec_registration_matches / _register_strategy_artifact now detect and reject (409) a register_if_absent collision that resolved to a different registry_id than requested (the unique_fields collision case).

split_api.py: register_if_absent binds a reserved _BOOTSTRAP_ACTOR (tenant=BUILTIN_TENANT) whenever it is called with no actor at all — the only such caller is strategy_artifact.py's ensure_builtin_strategy_artifacts at service bootstrap (every real HTTP route always passes a verified actor), so every checked-in built-in gets the reserved owner_tenant identity and is denied caller mutation by service.py's _authorize_write, without strategy_artifact.py itself needing to change (kept out of this task's declared artifact contract).

BFF strategy_adapter.py: _execute_update_params now always performs a follow-up scoped owner GET after the PATCH and verifies checksum/updated_at/metadata against the PATCH response before reporting success; an ambiguous/empty PATCH response now triggers that same readback to distinguish 'committed but response lost' (readback confirms the requested metadata: success, response_lost=True in the receipt) from 'not committed/unconfirmed' (raises ActionUnavailableError) instead of failing immediately without ever checking durable state.

test_strategy_artifact.py: test_strategy_artifact_advance_preserves_deployment_split rewritten to register and advance a fresh, non-builtin StrategyArtifact instead of mutating the shared built-in fixture (which the finding-1 fix now correctly denies).

test_owner_durability.py: pg_app fixture switched from a permissive structured-token stub to a strictly-signed HS256 JWT (issuer/audience/subject/tenant/role/expiry) — the finding-2 fail-closed-auth-config fix now correctly rejects the previous stub against the real Postgres backend this fixture selects.

test_strategy_registry_owner_prerequisite.py: updated call-count/method assertions to account for the adapter's new mandatory readback GET after the PATCH (previously asserted 'exactly one HTTP call', which the finding-5 fix intentionally changes to two).
